SOOPPIY DOCS — TRADING GATEWAY SETUP

Connect Upbit

How to create the API credentials at Upbit and connect them on the Accounts page. shadow first — live rollout in progress

1Before you start

  • An account at Upbit that has finished the venue's identity verification — an unverified account can create a key but cannot trade with it.
  • Two-factor authentication switched on at Upbit. Every venue asks for a 2FA code (and often an email confirmation) at the moment you create the key.
  • This page open next to the venue's site, and somewhere safe to hold the secret for the minute between creating it and connecting it.

2Availability and local rules

A Korean exchange operating under Korea's VASP registration. Practically it requires Korean residency, a Korean phone number and a linked K-Bank account for KRW deposits. Non-residents generally cannot complete verification.

Sooppiy does not decide who may use a venue — the venue's own KYC does, and your local law does. Connecting a gateway here does not make a venue available to you, and a venue you cannot legally use will simply refuse your key. This is factual guidance, not legal advice; access rules change, so confirm on the venue's own terms page for your country.

3What you need

  • API key
  • API secret
Grant TRADE permission only — never withdrawal. Use the venue's IP allowlist when it offers one. Start small. Your keys are encrypted at rest (AES-GCM) on Sooppiy's server and are never shown again after you save them.
IP restriction — leave it unset for now. Some venues let you lock a key to one server address. Sooppiy is moving its hosting region, and a key pinned to the old address would stop working the moment it moves. One consequence worth diarising: Binance and Bybit disable an unrestricted key's trading permission after 90 days, so plan to revisit the key then.

4Create your credentials at Upbit

  1. Log in at upbit.com → 마이페이지 (My Page) → Open API 관리 (Open API Management).
  2. Tick 자산조회 (asset inquiry) and 주문 (orders). Never the withdrawal permission.
  3. Upbit REQUIRES registering the calling server's IP address on the key — without it every request is refused.
The secret is shown exactly once, at creation. If you close that screen without copying it you cannot recover it — you have to delete the key and make a new one. Sooppiy never shows it again either, once saved.

5Where each value goes

At Upbit it is calledPaste it into Sooppiy's field
Access key (액세스 키)API key
Secret key (시크릿 키)API secret

6Connect it on the Accounts page

  1. Open Accounts → Trading gateway.
  2. Pick your region (ordering only — every broker stays available) and choose Upbit.
  3. Paste the credentials from step 2.
  4. Read and accept the live-trading terms — required even if you only plan to use shadow.
  5. Press Connect gateway. The account starts in paper mode: nothing is sent to Upbit yet.
  6. Switch the account to shadow (recommended first) or live on the account card.

7After you connect

  1. The gateway appears under Connected gateways with a health line. Key-pair venues show “credentials on file” — normal, it means there is no session to probe.
  2. Your automation rules do not switch by themselves. A rule only reaches Upbit when you set that rule's account type to shadow or live.
  3. Start in shadow and read the Drift records panel for a few days before considering live.
  4. To revoke access at any time, delete the key at Upbit — that stops every order instantly, whatever Sooppiy is set to.

8What each mode does with Upbit

ModeWhat happens
paperpaper / simulator — every trade stays on Sooppiy's internal ledger. Upbit is never contacted.
shadowshadow — Upbit has no sandbox and no dry-run call, so shadow makes no network call at all: your rule's intended orders are journalled against live book prices for the rollout soak, and nothing ever reaches Upbit. The journal rows appear in the drift panel with status “journal”.
livelive — not yet open for Upbit: the venue is in its shadow rollout soak, and live routing is refused with an explicit message until Sooppiy enables it platform-wide. Your rules can run in shadow meanwhile. Newly enabled venues also carry a $1,000 per-order limit at first (over-limit orders are refused, never resized).
Whatever mode you use, the Broker orders and Drift records panels at the bottom of the Accounts page show what Upbit actually confirmed next to what the ledger assumed — differences are surfaced loudly, never auto-corrected.

9Venue notes

  • KRW markets (KRW-BTC style). Your ledger stays in USD: Sooppiy records the KRW/USD rate it used on every order, taken from Upbit's own KRW-USDT book at that moment — and refuses to trade if no rate is available.
  • Upbit market buys are placed as a KRW amount (not a coin quantity); the coin volume actually bought is read back from the venue and any difference shows in the drift records.

10Troubleshooting

SymptomWhat it means / what to do
“credentials are missing or cannot be decrypted”The stored key can no longer be read (for example after a server key rotation). Reconnect the broker with fresh credentials.
“live-trading terms have not been accepted”Accept the terms for this broker on the Accounts page — consent is recorded per broker.
“not yet enabled for live orders on this platform”The venue is still in its shadow rollout. Shadow works today; live opens when the soak completes.
“no_authorization_ip” / every request 401The calling server's IP is not registered on the key. Add it in Upbit's Open API management.
“could not fetch KRW/USD rate — order refused”Upbit's KRW-USDT ticker was unreachable at that moment. The order is refused rather than guessed; it will be retried on the rule's next cycle.
